latest.title: Microsoft Teams Optimisation on Amazon WorkSpaces - Setup, Validation and Troubleshooting
latest.description: This post explains Microsoft Teams optimisation for Amazon WorkSpaces, where media is offloaded from the WorkSpace to the user's endpoint for better call quality and lower WorkSpace CPU. It covers what the capability is and how it works, prerequisites and setup on both the WorkSpace and the connecting device, validation on each side and in a live call, and troubleshooting using status indicators, the monitoring JSON, error codes and logs.

latest.title: Your Agent's Worst Bug Is Its Prompt. Here's How to Prove the Fix
latest.description: A hands-on guide to improving an AI agent using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Optimization. You analyze real traces, let the service recommend a better prompt from what actually failed, version the before and after as Configuration Bundles, and prove the improvement with a real A/B test. The running example is a code-security agent that reviews pull requests.

latest.title: Building Ephemeral GitHub Actions Self-Hosted Runners on AWS Fargate with Webhook-Driven Auto-Scaling
latest.description: Stop paying for idle runners. Deploy ephemeral GitHub Actions runners on AWS Fargate that launch only when jobs are queued and self-terminate after execution; pay only for actual CI/CD compute time. Security-first: KMS encryption, VPC endpoints, egress-only networking, HMAC-validated webhooks, and least-privilege IAM. No persistent infrastructure, no attack surface when idle.

latest.title: Debugging a Memory Leak with Kiro
latest.description: This post walks through using Kiro to diagnose and fix a memory leak in a Node.js application. We'll see how Kiro identifies common leak patterns, explains why they leak, and suggests concrete fixes you can apply immediately.

latest.description: This is a build I am currently building locally and learning how to build architectures . This article serves as a  reference pattern for what I am building behind the scenes bridging cloud-native architecture with the new global standard for payment messaging.

latest.title: Your Lambda MicroVM Images Have CVEs Nobody Can See — Closing the Loop with Inspector, Step Functions, and AWS DevOps Agent
latest.description: Lambda MicroVM images never touch a registry, so no scanner ever re-checks them for new CVEs. This post builds the "scan-twin" pattern that restores continuous visibility, then automates everything from finding to fix — AI-analyzed issues, a self-opening merge request, and Inspector-verified closure — for about $3/month, with the human merge as the only manual step.
